record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Achieve a full understanding of the relationship between input-to-state stability and integral input-to-state stability for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This asks for a general structural picture, not just isolated positive or negative examples.

evidence.quote: • Full understanding of relations between ISS and integral ISS for linear systems with unbounded operators is still missing.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider linear control systems of the form
  ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) space, A : D(A) ⊂ X → X generates a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on X, and B ∈ L(U, X_{-1}) is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator with U a Banach space and X_{-1} the extrapolation space associated with A. Inputs u are taken from L^∞_loc([0,∞); U).

Such a system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and θ, μ ∈ K_∞ such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + θ(∫₀^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds)  for all t ≥ 0.

Provide a complete structural characterization of the relationship between ISS and iISS for this class of linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded admissible input operators B. Specifically, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of (A, B, X, U), under which ISS implies iISS, under which iISS implies ISS, and identify the precise gap between the two notions in this setting (going beyond isolated examples and counterexamples to a general theory).
artifact.category_tag: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional linear systems
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint develops integral-to-integral ISS admissibility theory for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators, advancing the topic. While the bounded-B case is well understood (ISS and iISS coincide via exponential stability), a general structural characterization for unbounded admissible B remains incomplete; recent literature explicitly notes the question is much harder and several notorious sub-questions persist.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability in integral norms for linear infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: We study integral-to-integral input-to-state stability for infinite-dimensional linear systems... developing the corresponding admissibility theory for linear systems with unbounded input operators.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work advances but does not fully settle the ISS/iISS relationship for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Full understanding of relations between ISS and integral ISS for linear systems with unbounded operators is still missing.
status_evidence.claim: The survey explicitly lists this as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Integral input-to-state stability of unbounded bilinear control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies iISS for bilinear systems with unbounded operators; partial results extend to linear settings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists but a complete structural picture is not established.
